correctness.rationale: With axis e=(1,1,1)/sqrt(3), the Weyl chamber is a longitude lune of aperture pi/3 and probability 1/6; full-sphere normalized harmonics through degree two give nine orthonormal modes. Reflecting azimuth and axis parity splits the restricted Gram into explicit blocks A(4), B(2), C(2), D(1). Direct beta-function integrals int z^(2k)(1-z^2)^(q/2) and cosine/sine longitude integrals yield the stated entries. The source verifier symbolically regenerates all entries and characteristic polynomials; rational enclosures for pi and sqrt(3) yield disjoint sign-changing brackets exhausting 4+2+2+1 roots, proving simplicity/strict order and positivity rather than just floating values. Independent block-matrix eigensolving reproduced all nine decimals, trace exactly 1.5 and sqrt(lambda_max/lambda_min)=45.294...; a separate smooth quadrature checked the geometry at lower accuracy. Addition theorem gives trace=9/6.
